date.as_written: nepālaparṣagrahasiddhiśaine māsasite śrāvaṇike viśākhe | tithau dine sūte dine

notes: The chronogram 'nepālaparṣa(=varṣa) graha(9) siddhi(8) śaine(=śaila, 7)' gives NS 789 (c. 1669 CE), which matches the catalogue. The verse is corrupt. 'tithau dine sūte dine' gives no clear tithi or weekday; 'sūte' might stand for sūrya- (Sunday), but this is unverified. 'calilekhakāvyaṃ' probably hides a verb such as 'alīlikhat/alikhat kāvyaṃ' ('wrote the poem'). The scribe's name follows the catalogue (Dvijarūpa). Another possible reading is 'a dvija (brahmin) named Rūpa', with the name Rūpa and the title dvija. The canto is called 'navaviṃśatis' (29th), but the numeral is 19. The Agnivarṇa canto is the 19th, so read ekonaviṃśatitamaḥ.
